notes: Two supplied words are marked added here: the relative which of which is the year of tithing, and the object pronoun it after shalt give. The competing reading takes which is as one construction-supplied relative frame belonging to the appositional noun, on the analogy of rule 41; but rule 41 governs an adjective or participle, not an appositional noun, so the surplus subordinator is marked and only the copula joins the predicate under rule 20.
In šᵉnaṯ hammaʿăśēr the article stands on the rectum and the ASV renders the rectum anarthrously, so English fronts the single the and the article takes it (rule 29).
The apodosis writes its own waw, which carries the ASV's then (rule 14).
